- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or volatility.
- Forecasts tend to be too low during periods of strong upward momentum (e.g., 48.12, 49.30, 51.55) and fail to capture the full magnitude of the spike.
- Model shows persistent lag in recognizing true price peaks — often forecasting a peak too early or too low.
- After a spike, model tends to overshoot the mean or overcorrect, then undercorrect — suggesting a failure to model mean reversion properly.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the first 5–7 days of the horizon, then gradually increase — but often miss the true turning point or peak.
- Model exhibits a strong bias toward smoothing out volatility, underestimating the true variance in price movements.
- In cases where true price rises sharply, model fails to adjust forecast upward quickly enough — suggesting poor sensitivity to recent high volatility.
- Model tends to overestimate the “recovery” phase after a dip, often forecasting a rebound too early or too aggressively.
- Forecasts are often too low in the final 5–7 days of the horizon, especially when true price is rising — suggesting a failure to anticipate late-stage momentum.
- Model underestimates the impact of recent high prices on future forecasts — fails to “look ahead” from the current peak.
